title: EPR in Poland 2026: BDO, packaging, WEEE and batteries. What sellers need to know
summary: Who must register in BDO, what it costs (PLN 200/800), reporting packaging by material, the 1 Mg de minimis threshold, the 15 March deadline, WEEE, batteries and how EPR differs from PPWR.
text: ← All articles Selling to Poland without a local warehouse, office or subsidiary does not remove Polish EPR duties. A single product can trigger several obligations at once, and from 12 August 2026 PPWR adds another layer of packaging requirements. Here is what every seller to the Polish market needs to know. What EPR in Poland is Producers placing certain products or packaged goods on the Polish market may have to finance collection, recycling or recovery, keep records and report data. There is no single “Polish EPR number” that covers everything. Scope depends on the product and the company’s role in the supply chain. Covered areas include packaging, electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE), batteries and accumulators , plus selected products such as tyres, oils and certain single-use plastics. The central register is BDO, the database for products, packaging and waste management. Who must register in BDO The key question is who places the product or packaging on the Polish market , not where the company is based. That can include Polish manufacturers, non-EU importers, intra-EU acquirers, brand owners and foreign online or marketplace sellers shipping directly to Polish customers. Selling through a marketplace or a webshop does not by itself decide responsibility. The actual sales and logistics model has to be assessed. Example: an online electronics store A German company sells an LED lamp with a built-in battery to a Polish consumer. The lamp comes in a cardboard box with plastic film, shipped in an extra carton. One sale triggers four areas of obligations : WEEE The lamp is electrical equipment. Batteries The built-in battery is a separate stream. Product packaging The box and the film. Shipping packaging The extra carton is packaging to report as well. BDO registration is only the beginning Registration gives you a BDO number, but it does not mean all obligations are met. The entry must cover the right activities and streams . A company handling packaging, electronics and batteries may need entries in several areas. BDO registration cost in 2026 micro-enterprise PLN 200 annual fee. other businesses PLN 800 annual fee. The annual fee is the same every year and is generally due by the end of February. No extra annual fee is due in the year you paid the registration fee. The BDO fee is not the full cost, though. Depending on the stream, you may also pay a recovery organisation, recycling, education campaigns, collection obligations or product fees. Packaging EPR in Poland Reporting covers product, grouped, transport and e-commerce shipping packaging. Total parcel weight is not enough. Data must be split by material : paper and cardboard, plastics, glass, steel, aluminium, wood. 180 g cardboard 12 g film 25 g paper filling 3 lines reported separately At thousands of orders, that breakdown quickly becomes unmanageable in spreadsheets. Does a small volume exempt you? Poland has a de minimis mechanism for small packaging volumes, with a threshold of 1 Mg (1 tonne) per year . It is not a general EPR exemption. Relief from some financial duties does not necessarily remove registration, record-keeping or reporting, and using de minimis aid requires meeting formal conditions. Data to collect Good reporting starts well before the deadline and links sales data with product and packaging records: Product or SKU identification and sales market. Number of units sold. Packaging components and the material of each. Weight of each component. The correct EPR category, plus WEEE- and battery-specific data. Reporting deadline: 15 March The annual report on products, packaging and waste is filed electronically in BDO. The standard deadline is 15 March for the previous calendar year . Filing doesn’t always close the process: separate deadlines may apply to fees, recovery organisation documents and stream-specific duties. WEEE in Poland Companies placing electrical or electronic equipment on the market must assess WEEE obligations separately. Key questions: does the product meet the definition of equipment, and who places it on the market. Reporting may require the correct equipment category and weight. Selling small devices online does not create an automatic exemption . Batteries as a separate stream A battery built into a device is still its own compliance item. Batteries are a separate EPR stream, so one SKU can appear in WEEE, battery and packaging data at once. EU Regulation 2023/1542 on batteries is becoming more important while Poland adapts its national rules. Check the current procedure for your sales model and battery type. EPR and PPWR are two different layers PPWR · Regulation (EU) 2025/40 Covers the packaging itself: technical documentation, declaration of conformity, design, substances, and later recyclability and labelling. Applies from 12 August 2026. Polish EPR Registration, records, reporting and financing for packaging placed on the Polish market. PPWR does not remove national EPR duties. The same box, bottle or mailer is subject to both layers . Checklist before selling in Poland Identify covered products and who places them on the Polish market. Assess packaging, WEEE and batteries separately. Confirm the required BDO registration scope. Build SKU-level product and packaging data. Link that data to actual sales into Poland before calculating volumes and reports. How EPRPilot helps The hard part is rarely a single form. It is managing hundreds or thousands of SKUs across several markets, each needing different data. title: EPR and PPWR on marketplaces: where listing blocks are really coming
summary: Amazon, TikTok Shop, Zalando, eBay, Kaufland, Allegro and more: who already blocks listings without an EPR number, who is preparing, and what to do before Article 45 PPWR.
text: ← All articles Since PPWR started to apply on 12 August 2026, marketplaces have become one of the most visible enforcement points for EPR in European e-commerce. Amazon removes offers without registration numbers, TikTok Shop deactivates non-compliant listings and Zalando has set a date for blocking partner assortments. Platforms are at different stages, though. The key lesson: no block today does not mean no obligation tomorrow. Three levels of marketplace readiness Level 1 · enforcement Amazon, TikTok Shop and, in selected areas, Zalando. Missing data can already cost you sales. Level 2 · rollout Kaufland, eBay, bol.com and Zalando in further markets. Platforms collect data, build validation or announce consequences. Level 3 · preparation Allegro, eMAG and many others. Automated checks are held back mainly by national registries, but verification is being built. Amazon: the most advanced enforcement Amazon has been building EPR mechanisms for years, so PPWR did not mean starting from scratch. EPR numbers (ERN) go into the Regulatory Compliance section of Seller Central. The field only appears for markets where verification has launched. For Poland, Amazon told sellers to obtain a packaging number and warned that not registering before 12 August could lead to listing removal. Don’t wait for an Account Health warning. If you are an EPR producer, register whether or not the field is active yet . TikTok Shop: no number, no listing TikTok Shop’s instructions require packaging producers to hold a valid EPR number in every required market, appoint an authorised representative where needed, join a producer responsibility organisation and submit the number via Seller Center. Non-compliant listings can be deactivated and return only once a valid number is approved. It is a clear move to a chain: number → verification → permission to sell . Zalando: a firm blocking date of 1 January 2027 Zalando Partner is one of the most transparent platforms. EPR data is submitted through zDirect. It started with Germany, France and Spain, and since 12 August 2026 also covers Poland, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Hungary, Lithuania, Slovakia and Sweden. Zalando says partners who don’t submit the required EPR data by 1 January 2027 will have their assortment blocked. Fashion sellers may also have battery, textile and other obligations. Zalando already blocks battery products until compliance is verified. eBay and Kaufland: the infrastructure is ready eBay · listings can be hidden The packaging EPR number is added at account level: country, Packaging category, number and confirmation. Listings may be hidden if it is missing or invalid. Mass PPWR blocking across all EU countries could not be confirmed as of September 2026. Kaufland · EPR Compliance section Sellers pick a country and EPR category, enter the number and submit it for review. Kaufland refers to Article 45 PPWR. A packaging number is currently required in Germany, Poland, France and Spain. A note on Kaufland: a missing field in the panel for a country does not mean there is no EPR obligation there. bol.com, Allegro and eMAG: preparing, not blocking yet bol.com Not yet running mass verification of PPWR registrations, because there is no system to check against. In August 2026 it announced future checks and a possible impact on sales. Allegro A missing EPR number does not block sales for now, as EU countries are adapting their registries. The target is to check the number for every destination country before enabling sales. In September 2026 it started working with Interzero on EPR for exporting sellers. eMAG Covers producer registration, EPR fulfilment, authorised representatives and data submission. Self-certification is enough today, with verification extended as registries go live. Temu, AliExpress, OTTO OTTO has long required VerpackG system participation and ZSVR registration, but there is no strong confirmation of new PPWR-based blocks. Treat claims of blocks on Temu or AliExpress with caution until a credible source appears. Article 45 PPWR: why mass verification is coming Article 45 PPWR requires platforms to collect information on producers and their EPR compliance. The EU is working on a harmonised format for producer registries, and the Commission’s implementing documents expect automated, mass verification of registration numbers. Some marketplaces are not blocking yet because national infrastructure is missing , not because they don’t want to. Once registries become interoperable, enforcement can speed up sharply. What a cross-border seller should do now The most common mistake is thinking “the marketplace hasn’t blocked me, so I don’t need to do anything”. The legal obligation and platform enforcement are separate. The duty can exist before the platform is able to check it. Build a country × marketplace × EPR stream map and answer for each market: Is the company a producer under EPR/PPWR? Is packaging EPR registration required? Is an authorised representative needed? Does the product also fall under WEEE, batteries, textiles or another stream? Which numbers do you hold, and where must they be submitted? Does the marketplace already verify the number? Which packaging do you report: product, grouped, shipping? Do you have material and weight data and PPWR documentation? Who owns shipping packaging in marketplace fulfilment? Zalando says that under ZFS it takes responsibility for the shipping packaging it adds, while product packaging stays with the relevant EPR producer. bol.com describes a similar split for Logistics via bol. The implication: your data must separate product packaging from fulfilment packaging , and you must know who reports which component in which country. title: EUDR in Poland: penalties of up to 4% of turnover. What are the obligations?
summary: Who EUDR covers, what the Polish draft act UC101 changes, due diligence and the DDS, which authorities will inspect, what penalties apply and when the rules start.
text: ← All articles Many businesses still don’t realise they may be subject to EUDR. The obligations reach beyond importers of wood, coffee and cocoa to furniture producers and distributors, paper goods makers, sellers of seasonal products and makers of components containing wood or rubber. Poland’s draft act (UC101) adds no new substantive duties. It builds the national enforcement system: who inspects, how, and what penalties apply. EUDR is not only about wood importers EUDR, Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, covers cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya and wood , plus certain products made from them. wood furniture, paper rubber tyres, seals coffee · cocoa food soya · palm oil feed, cosmetics cattle leather, meat Scope is decided by Annex I and the product’s CN code , not simply by whether a commodity is in the product. Furniture, paper, e-commerce and manufacturing firms are often in scope without knowing it. First step: list your products, record their CN codes and check them against the current Annex I. What the Polish draft act UC101 changes The draft creates no new obligations, because those come directly from the EU regulation. It sets up national enforcement: control authorities, procedures and penalties. The draft has been revised several times, with versions at the Government Legislation Centre in April, July and August 2026, so penalty and procedure details may still change before it reaches parliament. Waiting for the final text is risky , because collecting supplier data and building records takes months. What the obligations are: due diligence Before placing a product on the market or exporting it, a covered business must run a due diligence process in four steps: 01 · information Product and supplier data, including where raw materials come from. 02 · risk assessment Risk of deforestation, forest degradation and breaches of the production country’s laws. 03 · risk mitigation Action wherever the assessment shows possible non-compliance. 04 · DDS Submitting a due diligence statement in the EUDR Information System. Who will supervise businesses in Poland The draft splits competences between several authorities: Veterinary Inspection Cattle. IJHARS Agri-Food Trade Quality Inspection: cocoa, coffee, soya and palm oil. Environmental Protection Inspection Wood and rubber. One company may deal with different authorities depending on the product flow. An importer with a broad range should know which authority covers which stream. What penalties apply The draft provides for sanctions showing that enforcement won’t stop at fines: Administrative fines based on turnover. A maximum fine of at least 4% of annual EU-wide turnover . The regulation requires this for legal persons, and the act will define how turnover is measured. Seizure and confiscation of goods. A ban on placing products on the market. A ban on exports. Temporary exclusion from public procurement. Temporary exclusion from grants and public funds. Is your company covered by EUDR? Check whether your products or imports contain, or are made from, wood, paper, rubber, coffee, cocoa, soya or palm oil. For each product group: Check CN codes against Annex I. Map suppliers and establish where raw materials come from in each flow. Identify your role: upstream operator, downstream operator or trader. Confirm the application date for your company size and product. Plan supplier data, record-keeping and due diligence documentation. Timelines: when EUDR applies 30.12.2026 · large and medium Full application of EUDR. 30.06.2027 · micro and small For most products. 30.12.2026 · exception Micro and small businesses with products already covered by EUTR stay on 30 December 2026. 30.12.2027 · added products Products added by delegated regulation, as indicated by the Commission. Check your company status, the specific product and transitional provisions. Collecting geolocation, assessing risk and building records usually take months, so start now. title: PPWR heavy metals limit: is a supplier’s “below 100 ppm” statement enough?
summary: A supplier’s one-page statement that packaging contains less than 100 ppm of heavy metals may be too vague for a PPWR technical file. What it should contain and when you need a test.
text: ← All articles Your supplier sends a one-page statement: “the packaging contains less than 100 ppm of heavy metals”. Job done? Often not. A statement like this is usually too vague to support a PPWR technical file. Here is what the limit actually requires, what a typical statement leaves out, and how to collect evidence that holds up in an inspection. What exactly does the 100 ppm limit mean? PPWR keeps the limit known from the Packaging Directive: 100 mg/kg in total for four metals: lead, cadmium, mercury and hexavalent chromium. It is a sum, not a limit for each metal. If lead is 60 mg/kg and cadmium 50 mg/kg, the packaging fails, even though each result looks fine on its own. The limit applies to the packaging and to each of its components . A compliant bottle does not “average out” a non-compliant cap or label. Every component is assessed separately. Pb lead Cd cadmium Hg mercury Cr(VI) hexavalent chromium Σ ≤ 100 mg/kg per component Which packaging is covered? PPWR’s scope is broad: all packaging placed on the EU market, whatever the material or sector. Sales, grouped and transport packaging, B2C and B2B. Passing the 100 ppm check does not mean full compliance. REACH restrictions and food-contact rules, among others, apply alongside PPWR and can set stricter conditions for specific substances. Why a bare “below 100 ppm” is not enough A typical statement has gaps that only show up during an inspection or a customer request: It doesn’t name the component. “Our packaging” is not the version 3 cap with colourant X. It doesn’t say whether it is the sum. You can’t tell if the result covers the combined four metals or each one separately. It gives no basis. Is it a test result, a calculation from the formulation, or a statement “from experience”? It has no date or version. The supplier changes raw materials, while the 2022 statement still sits in the binder. The documentation must trace back to exactly the component that goes into your packaging. What a useful supplier statement should contain The issuer and the person signing it. The exact component reference: specification number, item code, version and, if relevant, batch. A clear statement that the result covers the sum of Pb, Cd, Hg and Cr(VI), or results for each metal. The evidence basis: an accredited laboratory report or a documented formulation calculation. Dates: issue date, test date and validity. A commitment to notify you of changes to raw materials, suppliers or processes. A language your team understands, and readiness to make documents available to authorities. Does every component need a laboratory test? No. PPWR does not require one test per component. A risk-based approach makes sense: higher risk → test Recycled inputs, intense pigments and inks, printed elements, metal fittings, components from new or unproven suppliers. lower risk → formulation data Stable virgin materials with a controlled formulation, a track record of results and a contract to report changes. Four practical scenarios 01 · virgin PP closure Locked formulation, metal-free colourant, the same supplier for years. A statement based on the formulation plus a change clause is enough, with periodic testing, e.g. once a year. 02 · brightly coloured recycled crate Recyclate can carry old lead or cadmium pigments. You need batch testing and a check whether the crate falls under the crates and pallets derogation. 03 · printed paper label Paper is rarely the problem, inks and varnishes can be. Ask the printer for ink data and a result for the finished label. 04 · private label imported from outside the EU Often nobody has the full component list. As the brand owner you may be the manufacturer under PPWR, so collecting evidence and issuing the declaration is on you. Exceptions that need separate review Existing derogations, including for certain glass packaging and for plastic crates and pallets in closed loops, remain until they are amended or repealed. The Commission may lower the limit or change the derogations through delegated acts. Check the current status before relying on one. Who carries the final responsibility? The supplier provides evidence, but the packaging manufacturer carries out the conformity assessment, prepares the technical documentation and issues the EU Declaration of Conformity. In private-label models the brand owner may be the manufacturer. Importers must verify that this work has been done. Documentation is kept for 5 years for single-use packaging and 10 years for reusable packaging. Checklist before 12 August 2026 Break each pack down into components: body, closure, label, adhesive, ink, fittings. Assign a supplier and specification number to each component. Collect evidence that covers the sum of all four metals. Rank components by risk and commission tests where needed. Add change-notification clauses to supplier contracts. Store evidence against the exact item code and version. Review derogations and REACH and food-contact requirements. title: PPWR importer obligations: what changes when your manufacturer is outside the EU
summary: Buying from a supplier in China, the UK, Turkey or the US? Under PPWR you are the importer. Who counts as importer, core duties, when you become the manufacturer, and EPR.
text: ← All articles Buying packaged goods from a supplier in China, the UK, Turkey or the US? Under PPWR that makes you the importer, and a large part of the manufacturer’s responsibility shifts onto you. Regulation (EU) 2025/40 on packaging and packaging waste (PPWR) applies from 12 August 2026. It replaced Directive 94/62/EC and applies directly, with no national transposition, so the same rules work in all 27 member states. Role allocation surprises companies most: manufacturer, authorised representative, importer and distributor. When the manufacturer is outside the EU, the market surveillance authority contacts the importer. Who counts as an importer under PPWR An importer is an EU-established natural or legal person that first places on the EU market packaging or a packaged product from a third country. Your core business doesn’t matter. If you import shampoo in bottles, the bottles, caps, labels, cartons and pallet wrap are your packaging. 01 · brand sourcing in Asia Imports finished goods and sells them under its own name. 02 · distributor or wholesaler Buys directly from non-EU suppliers. 03 · online seller Brings stock into an EU fulfilment centre. 04 · component imports Parts arrive in transport packaging, which is also covered by PPWR. Your core obligations Before placing packaging on the market, you must check that the non-EU manufacturer has complied, and be able to prove it: Confirm the conformity assessment was carried out and an EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation exist. Check correct material identification and sorting labels. Make sure manufacturer and importer details appear on the packaging or accompanying documents. Keep the declaration of conformity and technical documentation for 5 years and provide them on request. Ensure storage and transport don’t compromise compliance. If packaging is non-compliant, take corrective action, withdraw or recall it and inform the authorities. When the importer becomes the manufacturer A rule familiar from other EU product law applies. You take on full manufacturer obligations if you place packaging under your own name or trademark, or modify packaging already on the market in a way that affects its conformity. Private-label importers are almost always in this position. Then you, not your supplier, own the technical documentation, conformity assessment, recyclability performance grade and recycled-content evidence. Read more in our post on PPWR and private label . EPR on top: Articles 44 and 45 As the first entity placing packaging on a national market, the importer is also the EPR producer in that country. That means: Registration An entry in the national producer register. Authorised representative Where the country requires one. Annual reports Packaging placed on the market by material and weight. Fees Eco-modulated fees depending on the type of packaging. All of it is per country . Selling into 8 EU markets means 8 registrations, 8 fee schedules and 8 reporting calendars, each with different deadlines, units and material categories. The 10-day request you should expect The first PPWR pressure will more likely come from customers than inspectors. Retailers and B2B buyers are adding contract clauses requiring a declaration of conformity within short deadlines, often 10 working days . When supplier data is scattered across e-mails and spreadsheets, that deadline is very hard to meet. Importer readiness checklist Map every SKU to its packaging components, materials and weights. Collect supplier declarations, recycled-content evidence and recyclability data. Identify which group entity is the legal importer in each market. Confirm EPR registrations in every country you sell to. Set up a repository that produces a declaration of conformity in days, not weeks. Add PPWR clauses to purchase contracts with non-EU suppliers. title: PPWR and private label: when your brand becomes the packaging manufacturer
summary: Under PPWR the packaging manufacturer is often the brand owner, not the factory. Roles, supplier contracts, required evidence, scenarios and a private-label checklist.
text: ← All articles Outsourcing production does not outsource responsibility. Under PPWR, Regulation (EU) 2025/40, who is responsible for packaging depends on the role a company plays and the name or trademark under which the packaging is placed on the market, not on who sends the production invoice. In many private-label models, the brand owner is the manufacturer for compliance purposes. The factory is not always the legal manufacturer Article 3(1)(13) PPWR defines the manufacturer broadly. It includes anyone who has packaging or a packaged product designed or manufactured under its own name or trademark , even if another trademark is also visible. Example: factory A makes a washing-up liquid bottle, co-packer B fills it and retailer C sells it under its own brand. Retailer C may carry the manufacturer’s duties without owning a single machine. Roles have to be checked against contracts, branding, the supply route and who first places the packaging on the EU market. A logo is a strong signal, but not the only one. Four roles companies often confuse One company can hold several roles at once: Supplier or co-packer Physically produces the packaging or packs the product and supplies technical evidence. Manufacturer under PPWR Responsible for conformity when packaging is placed on the market under its name or trademark. Importer Places non-EU packaging or packaged products on the EU market and checks that the manufacturer has complied. Producer for EPR Registers and finances packaging-waste obligations in each market it sells to. A European brand importing private-label cosmetics from outside the EU can be the manufacturer, the importer and the EPR producer at the same time. A supplier contract does not rewrite the regulation A clause saying “the supplier guarantees PPWR compliance” is useful, but it does not transfer statutory duties . Authorities can still address the brand owner as manufacturer, whatever the parties agreed between themselves. Contracts still matter. They secure access to test reports, change control, warranties, indemnities and recourse. They allocate commercial risk, but they don’t replace the legal allocation of roles. What works in practice is an evidence process : a list of required documents per packaging reference, approval rights for changes, deadlines for missing data and consequences for incomplete evidence. What a private-label manufacturer must be able to show Before packaging is placed on the market, Article 15 requires the manufacturer to carry out (or have carried out) the conformity assessment under Article 38, prepare technical documentation under Annex VII and collect evidence of compliance. A general supplier statement for a whole catalogue is rarely enough for a specific packaging reference. You need: a technical description of the packaging, components, materials and intended use, evidence for the applicable requirements: substances, recyclability, recycled content, packaging minimisation, the EU declaration of conformity under Article 39 and Annex VIII, a type, batch, serial or other identifier linking units on the market to the documentation, manufacturer contact details on the packaging or, where allowed, in an accompanying document, a controlled record of changes to suppliers, materials, design and test results. Four private-label scenarios 01 · retailer own brand A supermarket with own-brand food and household goods needs a controlled compliance file for every packaging family. 02 · D2C brand An online brand orders jars and cartons from several EU suppliers. It owns no factory, yet it may still be the manufacturer. 03 · non-EU sourcing A Polish company imports cosmetics from Asia. It has manufacturer and importer duties at once and cannot rely on a one-page “PPWR compliant” letter. 04 · supplier change A beverage brand changes a label, cap, adhesive or laminate. That can change composition, recyclability and the evidence behind the declaration, so the assessment must be reviewed before release. The narrow micro-enterprise exception PPWR contains a limited qualification for certain micro-enterprises with packaging made under their name or trademark. It can affect who counts as manufacturer when the supplier is in the same Member State. It is not a broad exemption : both the EU micro-enterprise criteria and the same-Member-State condition must be met, and cross-border or non-EU sourcing usually rules it out. Existing stock: placing on the market is what counts The production order date is not necessarily decisive. What matters is when each packaging unit was first placed on the EU market . Stock first placed on the market after the relevant PPWR requirements start to apply may have to meet them. Keep invoices, delivery records, batch data and supplier confirmations to defend your stock status in an inspection. What changes from 12 August 2026 PPWR generally applies from 12 August 2026, but individual requirements have their own dates and some depend on implementing acts or harmonised methods. Priorities now: map roles, prepare documentation, get usable supplier evidence, assign ownership of the conformity assessment and link each declaration to the right product, supplier and market. Private-label readiness checklist Map every own-brand SKU to its packaging components and references. Record who designs, manufactures, imports and first places each reference on the EU market. Confirm the legal manufacturer rather than relying on the internal “supplier” label. Request reference-specific technical data and test evidence. Set change-control rules for materials, dimensions, inks, adhesives and suppliers. Prepare and approve an EU declaration of conformity for each packaging family. Connect PPWR documentation with national packaging EPR registrations and reports. Keep evidence for the required period: generally 5 years, or 10 years for reusable packaging. title: PPWR supplier declarations: what actually counts as evidence?
summary: A company-wide “PPWR compliant” letter does not prove a packaging complies. What an EU declaration of conformity must contain (Art. 39, Annex VIII), red flags and what to ask suppliers for.
text: ← All articles Since PPWR, Regulation (EU) 2025/40, became generally applicable on 12 August 2026, buyers have been asking suppliers for a “PPWR declaration” and receiving company-wide PDFs. A letter like that does not prove that a specific packaging complies. Article 39(2) requires the EU declaration of conformity to follow the Annex VIII model, which identifies the specific packaging by a unique identification. Why are blanket “PPWR declarations” suddenly everywhere? The pattern is usually the same. A brand owner or distributor learns the regulation applies and e-mails every supplier. Suppliers have no conformity file per reference, so they send a quick letter saying the company takes the regulation seriously. The buyer files the letter and considers the job done. The result is an impression of compliance while no packaging is documented. Market surveillance, a large customer’s compliance team or lawyers in due diligence will review the file reference by reference. What an EU declaration of conformity under PPWR is It is a statement by the responsible operator, on its sole responsibility, that a specific packaging meets Regulation (EU) 2025/40. It is drawn up under Article 39 following the Annex VIII model and backed by technical documentation described in Annex VII. One declaration covers one packaging, never a whole company. A letterhead letter is about the company and proves nothing about any packaging. A marketing or scheme certificate, such as “certified sustainable packaging”, follows that scheme’s criteria. At most it can feed your technical file. Only a per-packaging declaration, together with data on materials, substances and recyclability, is usable evidence. What a valid declaration should contain Elements that follow from the Annex VIII model: A unique identification of the packaging: reference, name or description that maps to what you buy. Name and address of the operator taking responsibility. The full citation: Regulation (EU) 2025/40, not “applicable EU packaging rules”. A conformity statement about that packaging, not about company intentions or values. Place, date and a named signatory. The date matters when the packaging changes. Red flags not enough No packaging identified. “All our products” as scope. No regulation number. A marketing footer instead of a signature. a simple test If the same PDF could go to every customer unchanged, it does not identify your packaging. Does a supplier declaration replace your obligations? No. A supplier document is input evidence, not a transfer of responsibility . The operator placing the packaging on the market answers for its conformity. If that is you, you draw up your own declaration backed by your own Annex VII documentation. From suppliers you need data, not reassurance. Three families of data matter most: Composition Materials and their weights for each component. Substances · Art. 5 Including the 100 mg/kg limit for lead, cadmium, mercury and hexavalent chromium and the restriction on intentionally added PFAS in food-contact packaging. Design · Art. 6 Design data the recyclability assessment depends on. Read more about the heavy-metals limit in our post PPWR heavy metals limit . What to ask your supplier for instead Ask per packaging reference or SKU, not per company. Ask for a declaration that identifies that packaging and refers to the Annex VIII model. Ask for the supporting data: material composition by weight, Article 5 substances information, recyclability-relevant design data. Log missing items and refuse silent substitutions. A second letterhead PDF is not an answer. Make per-reference conformity documentation a contractual condition of purchase.
